title: Tricky Deal
reviewNotes: Verified the final maneuver after ...Re8, plus an independent king-retreat alternative and immediate-promotion draw. The earlier rook-check sequence remains source context.
transcript: White is only one step away from getting a new queen, but black has an entire rook for bishop and it is going to be pretty easy for him to stop the pawn. But at least you would think that because actually we can notice that if the rook goes to H8 and tries to stop the pawn like this, now after bishop to F6 there would be a fork picking up the rook and winning the game. So black has to be a little bit more careful and precise and give a check to white king first to try and change the line that it's going to move to. But now after the king moves, [music] black still needs to be careful because actually going to F8 would still be rushed because of the majestic resource bishop to F6, a beautiful sacrifice that cannot be accepted without allowing white to promote to a queen. But if the sacrifice is not taken, it means that black has to move the king and the only square that it can move to is C5, which would allow another fork and make white win again. So instead of this, black has to give one more check to white king, force it to move and then finally go to E8. Now the rook is on a light square so there is no way for the bishop to ever attack it. So surely this is it. Black is simply out of the woods, right? Well, not exactly. White can play the very precise bishop F2 check and once again force the black king to an only move to E5. And from here we can exploit the position of the black king to give another check and no matter where the king moves, the bishop is going to fly to B8 next covering the view of the rook with the help of the pawn preparing to promote and black is out of resources. He's going to have to give up the rook for the bishop and lose this beautiful end game.
